mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of instances where FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) when GDPC1 falls by more than 2% year-over-year.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the unemployment rate above 6% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of instances when UNRATE exceeds 6% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months signals supply-side stress, which raises input costs and suppresses earnings growth, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when INDPRO is below its 12-month MA for four consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL above their respective 12-month averages signals a dual tightening in monetary policy and inflation, which increases real interest rates and erodes equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL exceed their 12-month averages simultaneously.

mechanism_narrative: A strong positive correlation between HOUST and GDPC1 over the past six months indicates robust housing demand coinciding with overall economic expansion, which boosts consumer confidence and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: Pearson correlation(HOST, GDPC1) > 0.7 over last 6 months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive when the correlation between HOUST and GDPC1 exceeds 0.7 over the prior six months.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid acceleration in payroll employment growth (PAYEMS) above 0.5% month-over-month for two consecutive months signals a tight labor market and upward wage pressure, which compresses profit margins and ultimately leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when PAYEMS grows above 0.5% month-over-month for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in real personal savings (RSAFS) below its 12-month average for six consecutive months signals increased consumer reliance on debt to sustain spending, which raises default risk and ultimately produces negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when RSAFS is below its 12-month average for six consecutive months.
